 EXHIBIT 99.1
 Exhibit 99.1 
 | 
 Release 
 | 
 November 16, 2026
 TELUS confirms receipt of unsolicited
proposal from Québecor, continues review of strategic alternatives 
 Special Committee of independent
directors is reviewing the unsolicited Québecor proposal, has identified several significant regulatory and execution risks 
 Special Committee is also exploring strategic alternatives
in the best interests of TELUS 
 TELUS remains focused on the continued execution of its
transformation plan 
 Vancouver, British Columbia – TELUS Corporation
(TSX: T, NYSE: TU) today confirmed that its Board of Directors has received an unsolicited, non-binding, and conditional proposal from
Québecor regarding a transaction that would result in Québecor acquiring TELUS. The TELUS Board has formed a Special Committee
of independent directors and engaged both financial and legal advisors to carefully review and evaluate the Québecor proposal.
 John Manley, Chair of the TELUS Board of Directors, said,
“With the support of our advisors, the Special Committee is conducting a thorough review of Québecor’s proposal to
determine the course of action that will be in the best interests of TELUS and its stakeholders. To date, this review has surfaced a number
of significant risks associated with Québecor’s proposal, including the fact that more than four months after its initial
proposal, Québecor has yet to explain how what it is proposing could be approved under the current telecom regulatory framework
in Canada and that a regulatory review of such a transaction would be a long and costly process for our shareholders. That said, we are
prepared to continue our engagement with Québecor and its advisors, as well as government and applicable regulatory authorities,
in respect of the concerns raised.”
 “At the same time, the Special Committee is exploring
other strategic alternatives available to TELUS to maximize value for the company and its stakeholders while supporting Victor and his
leadership team in the continued execution of our transformation plan,” added Mr Manley.
 Significant Execution and Regulatory Risks Associated
with Unsolicited Québecor Proposal 
 The TELUS Board received the initial Québecor proposal
on June 27, 2026. Following receipt, TELUS engaged in dialogue with Québecor to clarify certain aspects of that proposal and address
its initial concerns with the terms of the proposed transaction. The TELUS Board then received an amended proposal from Québecor
on November 9, 2026. The Special Committee is considering the Québecor proposal as a whole, including the value it offers TELUS
and its shareholders, the regulatory approvals required, the proposed governance and ownership structure, the financing and resulting
leverage, and the conditions to which the proposal is subject.
 The Special Committee’s review
has identified significant regulatory and execution risks associated with the proposed Québecor transaction, the successful completion
of which would require multiple regulatory approvals which may not be obtained, or may only be obtained subject to conditions that materially
affect the combined company. 
 Importantly, Québecor’s proposal does not set
out the regulatory strategy Québecor would pursue, nor the remedies it would be prepared to accept to obtain those approvals. Existing
spectrum policy, the conditions on which recent wireless consolidation was approved, and amendments to the Competition Act give rise to
significant concerns regarding the timing, conditions and overall uncertainty associated with obtaining the required regulatory approvals.
As presented, Québecor’s proposal does not appropriately allocate these risks between the parties, such that the majority
would effectively be borne by TELUS and its shareholders. A prolonged regulatory review process would inevitably impose significant demands
on TELUS’ management and employees, create uncertainty for TELUS, its customers, employees, shareholders, and other stakeholders,
and constrain TELUS’ ability to pursue and execute its strategic plan, all without an appropriate degree of transaction certainty.
 In addition, the proposed governance structure raises significant
concerns. The proposal would result in Québecor gaining control of a combined entity in which TELUS shareholders would contribute
the majority of the economic value while receiving a minority voting position. Québecor’s controlling shareholder would achieve
voting control of the combined business and the right to designate a majority of directors while contributing a minority of the economic
value.
 The Board is also giving consideration to the fact that TELUS
shareholders would be asked to accept equity in a materially more leveraged enterprise, at a time when TELUS and its peers are focused
on deleveraging and when interest rates have, and may continue to, increase significantly. A highly levered combined company would be
less able to invest in its business, its people and in connecting communities in the markets TELUS serves across Canada.
 With respect to the financial terms, the Board is not satisfied
that the consideration offered under the proposal adequately reflects the value of TELUS, its leading position in the Canadian telecommunications
market nor the value creation opportunities available to TELUS through continued execution of TELUS’ strategic plan. The Board is
also concerned that the value ultimately realized by TELUS shareholders would remain uncertain. Québecor’s proposal contemplates
a fixed exchange ratio and therefore exposes TELUS shareholders to fluctuations in Québecor’s share price throughout the
extended regulatory review period that the proposed transaction would require. As a result, any premium implied by Québecor’s
proposal may differ materially from the value ultimately received by TELUS shareholders.
 Review of Strategic Alternatives 
 In addition to its review of the Québecor proposal,
the Special Committee is continuing a comprehensive review of strategic alternatives available to TELUS, including the continued execution
of the transformation plan under TELUS’ new leadership. This review is ongoing with a view to realizing TELUS’ full potential.
 As the Special Committee’s review progresses, TELUS
will remain focused on its plan to deliver sustainable long-term value to shareholders, including the strategic actions that are already
underway – building a stronger, more resilient business, growing free cash flow, and deploying capital more efficiently to deliver
profitable, sustainable growth and returns. The Board has full confidence in TELUS’ newly appointed President and Chief Executive
Officer, Victor Dodig, and in the management team to execute on TELUS’ strategic plan.
 The Special Committee is
continuing its evaluation of the Québecor proposal and the other strategic alternatives available to the company, and no
decision has been made at this time whether to pursue a transaction or maintain the status quo. The TELUS Board and its Special
Committee are committed to acting in the best interests of the company and its stakeholders, and will reach their conclusions on the
basis of a complete and careful consideration of all relevant matters, taking the time required to do so with the assistance of
TELUS’ financial and legal advisers.
 TELUS does not intend to issue or disclose
developments with respect to any of the above matters except as required under its regulatory obligations. There can be no assurance that
TELUS’ review of strategic alternatives will result in any transaction or that, if undertaken, such transaction would be completed.
 TD Securities Inc. and Stikeman Elliott LLP have been engaged
as financial and legal advisors, respectively, to the TELUS Board and the Special Committee.
 A copy of TELUS’ response letter transmitted to Québecor
on November 15, 2026 is as follows:
 November 15, 2026
 PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL 
 Mr. Pierre Karl Péladeau
 President and Chief Executive Officer
 Québecor Inc. 
 612, rue St-Jacques
 17e étage
 Montréal, Quebec H3C 4M8
 Dear Mr. Péladeau:
 Re: Québecor's non-binding proposals dated June
26, 2026 and November 9, 2026 
 The Board of Directors (the " Board ") of
TELUS Corporation (" TELUS ") has been carefully reviewing Québecor's June 26, 2026 non-binding proposal (the " Initial
Proposal ") and November 9, 2026 alternate non-binding proposal (the " Alternate Proposal " and, together with
the Initial Proposal, the " Proposal "), with the assistance of the special committee of independent directors established
for that purpose and the advice of its financial and legal advisers. This letter follows your discussion with Victor Dodig, President
and Chief Executive Officer of TELUS, on November 14, 2026 and Mr. Dodig's invitation to meet on November 23, 2026, together with the
Chief Financial Officers of our respective companies, to discuss the Proposal.
 In conducting its review, the Board is considering the strategic
rationale of the Proposal, its potential benefits and risks, the likelihood and implications of obtaining the required regulatory approvals,
the proposed governance framework and the value offered to TELUS shareholders, in each case against the opportunities available to TELUS
under its strategic plan and other reasonably available alternatives.
 The Board's principal concerns relate to three areas: (i)
the significant regulatory and execution uncertainty associated with the Proposal; (ii) the governance framework contemplated for the
combined company; and (iii) whether the value offered adequately reflects TELUS' intrinsic value, future prospects and the risks that
TELUS shareholders would be asked to assume.
 A
central consideration informing the Board's assessment is that, as currently structured, the Proposal would require TELUS shareholders
to bear a disproportionate share of the transaction's risks and uncertainties. These include regulatory approval risk, execution risk
and, in the case of the Initial Proposal, the risks associated with the proposed monetization of TELUS Health, while also exposing TELUS
shareholders to the uncertainty inherent in a fixed-exchange-ratio transaction expected to remain subject to an extended regulatory review
process. At the same time, TELUS shareholders would contribute the majority of the economic value of the combined company while holding
a minority voting position. 
 While the Board believes that the Proposal, in its current
form, does not adequately address the concerns outlined above, it remains open to continuing a constructive dialogue with Québecor
and its advisers regarding potential paths to addressing those concerns. The Board would also be prepared, where appropriate, to support
discussions with relevant governmental and regulatory authorities regarding the regulatory framework applicable to any potential transaction.
 | 1. | The Board is conducting a thorough and independent review
of the Proposal | 
 Following receipt of the Initial Proposal, the Board established
a special committee of independent directors (the " Special Committee "), chaired by the Chair of the Board, to oversee
the Board's review of the Initial Proposal (and subsequently the Alternate Proposal) and the alternatives reasonably available to TELUS.
The Special Committee and the Board are advised by TD Securities Inc. as financial adviser and Stikeman Elliott as legal counsel.
 With the assistance of the Board's advisers, the Special
Committee is conducting a comprehensive review of the Proposal, including its terms, conditions and underlying assumptions; evaluating
the Proposal against TELUS' strategic plan and other reasonably available alternatives; and assessing the regulatory, financing and execution
risks associated with the transaction contemplated by the Proposal. The Special Committee regularly reports its findings to the Board.
The Board's feedback set out in this letter is the product of that comprehensive review.
 By way of clarification, while you met in London with TELUS'
then Chief Executive Officer in November 2025 to present a preliminary concept for a potential combination, the TELUS Board was not meeting
at that time. Although the Board subsequently received the related materials, its consideration of the matter took place at a later meeting
following an appropriate briefing from management.
 Since that initial outreach, TELUS subsequently underwent
a significant change in its management team, announced on February 12, 2026 and effective July 1, 2026, and revised its dividend policy
and strategic plan. Given these circumstances, the time taken to undertake a thorough and extensive assessment of the Proposal is both
appropriate and warranted.
 | 2. | The Proposal is subject to substantial regulatory and
execution risk | 
 Based on the current regulatory framework, including existing
spectrum policy, the conditions on which recent wireless consolidation was approved and developments under the Competition Act, the Board
has significant concerns regarding the feasibility, timing, and conditions of obtaining the required regulatory approvals.
 Throughout its review, the Special Committee sought additional
information regarding Québecor's regulatory strategy, anticipated approval process, potential remedies and proposed allocation
of regulatory risk. While Québecor and its advisers engaged constructively with the Special Committee, the Board does not believe
it has been provided with a sufficiently clear basis to assess the likelihood, timing or consequences of obtaining the required approvals,
including the nature of any remedies that may ultimately be required and their impact on the combined company.
 In the Board's view, the Proposal also does not contain an
appropriate allocation of regulatory risk. As currently structured, TELUS shareholders would bear substantial uncertainty regarding both
the outcome of the approval process and the consequences of any conditions imposed, without corresponding protections should those approvals
not be obtained or be obtained only on burdensome terms.
 For
these reasons, the Board does not currently believe the Proposal, in its current form, provides a sufficiently clear path to completion.
The Board considers this issue fundamental and believes it should be addressed. At the same time, the Board does not view these concerns
as precluding further discussions and remains open to considering, once Québecor has set out how it proposes to obtain the required
approvals, whether a more certain and workable path to those approvals can be identified, including through discussions with relevant
governmental and regulatory authorities. 
 | 3. | The proposed governance structure raises significant concerns | 
 The Board also has significant concerns regarding the governance
framework contemplated by the Proposal. Under the proposed structure, TELUS shareholders would contribute the majority of the economic
value of the combined company while holding a minority voting interest. At the same time, Québecor's controlling shareholder would
obtain effective voting control of the combined company and the right to designate a majority of the board despite contributing a minority
of the combined company’s economic value.
 The Board views governance and shareholder rights as important
considerations in evaluating any transaction. Since the elimination of TELUS' dual-class share structure in 2013, TELUS has operated under
a one-share, one-vote model without a controlling shareholder. The Board believes that model appropriately aligns economic ownership and
voting power and promotes accountability to all shareholders.
 In the Board's view, the Proposal would represent a significant
departure from those principles and, as currently structured, does not provide sufficient value or other benefits to justify that outcome.
 | 4. | The Proposal raises significant concerns regarding value | 
 The Board is not satisfied that the consideration offered
under the Proposal adequately reflects the value of TELUS, its leading position in the Canadian telecommunications market nor the value
creation opportunities available to TELUS through continued execution of TELUS' strategic plan.
 The valuation implied by the Proposal compares unfavourably
to relevant Canadian telecommunications transaction precedents and does not, in the Board's view, provide an appropriate premium having
regard to TELUS' historical trading multiples, business profile and future prospects. The valuation implied by the Alternate Proposal
is similarly below those levels. In addition, under the Proposal, TELUS shareholders would receive a materially lower dividend following
completion of the transaction.
 The Board also notes that the premiums cited by Québecor
are highly sensitive to the reference dates and market conditions used in their calculation. The Initial Proposal did not represent a
meaningful premium to TELUS' trading price as recently as June 2026, while the premium cited in the Alternate Proposal is measured relative
to TELUS' closing share price on November 6, 2026 and is driven in significant part by changes in the relative trading performance of
TELUS and Québecor since June 2026. The Board further notes that both the Initial Proposal and the Alternate Proposal were made
during a period in which TELUS and Québecor were trading at historically unusual relative valuation levels, with TELUS shares trading
near multi-year lows relative to Québecor shares trading near all-time highs.
 The Board is also concerned that the value ultimately realized
by TELUS shareholders would remain uncertain. Under the Initial Proposal, that uncertainty arises in part from the proposed monetization
of TELUS Health at a specified valuation within a compressed timeframe and under significant public scrutiny. Under the Alternate Proposal,
TELUS Health would instead be included in the transaction, with the only incremental consideration being an increase in the exchange ratio
from 0.1600 to 0.1700 of a Québecor share. Based on Québecor's closing share price on November 6, 2026, that increase represents
approximately $0.77 per TELUS share, or approximately $1.2 billion in aggregate, compared to the approximately $5.4 billion value attributed
to TELUS Health in the Initial Proposal. More broadly, the Proposal contemplates a fixed exchange ratio and therefore exposes TELUS shareholders
to fluctuations in Québecor's share price throughout what is expected to be an extended regulatory review period. As a result,
any premium implied at signing may differ materially from the value ultimately received at closing.
 The Board is further
concerned that TELUS shareholders would be asked to exchange their ownership interest in TELUS for equity in a significantly more
leveraged enterprise. Based on Québecor's assumptions, the combined company would have pro forma net leverage of
approximately 4.1x estimated 2027 EBITDA. This would represent a significant increase in leverage at a time when TELUS and the
telecommunications sector are focused on deleveraging, maintaining financial flexibility and navigating higher interest rate
environment. In the Board's view, the resulting capital structure would materially reduce the combined
company's capacity to invest in its networks, workforce and long-term growth opportunities.
 Finally, the Board believes that a significant portion of
the value attributed to the Proposal is derived from assets, earnings and initiatives that TELUS shareholders already own or are expected
to benefit from under TELUS' strategic plan. TELUS is expected to contribute approximately 74% of the combined company's 2025 Adjusted

as precluding further discussions and remains open to considering, once Québecor has set out how it proposes to obtain the required
approvals, whether a more certain and workable path to those approvals can be identified, including through discussions with relevant
governmental and regulatory authorities. 
 | 3. | The proposed governance structure raises significant concerns | 
 The Board also has significant concerns regarding the governance
framework contemplated by the Proposal. Under the proposed structure, TELUS shareholders would contribute the majority of the economic
value of the combined company while holding a minority voting interest. At the same time, Québecor's controlling shareholder would
obtain effective voting control of the combined company and the right to designate a majority of the board despite contributing a minority
of the combined company’s economic value.
 The Board views governance and shareholder rights as important
considerations in evaluating any transaction. Since the elimination of TELUS' dual-class share structure in 2013, TELUS has operated under
a one-share, one-vote model without a controlling shareholder. The Board believes that model appropriately aligns economic ownership and
voting power and promotes accountability to all shareholders.
 In the Board's view, the Proposal would represent a significant
departure from those principles and, as currently structured, does not provide sufficient value or other benefits to justify that outcome.
 | 4. | The Proposal raises significant concerns regarding value | 
 The Board is not satisfied that the consideration offered
under the Proposal adequately reflects the value of TELUS, its leading position in the Canadian telecommunications market nor the value
creation opportunities available to TELUS through continued execution of TELUS' strategic plan.
 The valuation implied by the Proposal compares unfavourably
to relevant Canadian telecommunications transaction precedents and does not, in the Board's view, provide an appropriate premium having
regard to TELUS' historical trading multiples, business profile and future prospects. The valuation implied by the Alternate Proposal
is similarly below those levels. In addition, under the Proposal, TELUS shareholders would receive a materially lower dividend following
completion of the transaction.
